```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(infer)
library(randomForest)
library(tidymodels)
library(modelr)
library(dplyr)
library(yardstick)
library(pROC)
load('../data/biomarker-clean.RData')
```

```{r}
## MULTIPLE TESTING
####################

# function to compute tests
test_fn <- function(.df){
  t_test(.df, 
         formula = level ~ group,
         order = c('ASD', 'TD'),
         alternative = 'two-sided',
         var.equal = F)
}

# partition into training and test set
# done before any testing or protein selection to ensure all when constructing model is based entirely on the testing set and not the whole data set
set.seed(1268)
biomarker_split <- biomarker_clean %>%
  initial_split(prop = 0.8)

ttests_out <- training(biomarker_split) %>%
  # drop ADOS score
  select(-ados) %>%
  # arrange in long format
  pivot_longer(-group, 
               names_to = 'protein', 
               values_to = 'level') %>%

# nest by protein
nest(data = c(level, group)) %>% 
  # compute t tests
  mutate(ttest = map(data, test_fn)) %>%
  unnest(ttest) %>%
  # sort by p-value
  arrange(p_value) %>%
  # multiple testing correction
  mutate(m = n(),
         hm = log(m) + 1/(2*m) - digamma(1),
         rank = row_number(),
         p.adj = m*hm*p_value/rank)
``` 


```{r}
## RANDOM FOREST
##################

# store predictors and response separately
predictors <- training(biomarker_split) %>%
  select(-c(group, ados))

response <- training(biomarker_split) %>% 
  pull(group) %>% 
  factor()

# fit RF
set.seed(1268)
rf_out <- randomForest(x = predictors, 
                       y = response, 
                       ntree = 1000, 
                       importance = T)

# check errors
rf_out$confusion
```

```{r}
#Model Generator function used later for testing several combinations of parameters
modelGenerators <- function(num1, num2, intersection = FALSE){
  proteins_s1 <- ttests_out %>%
    slice_min(p.adj, n = num1) %>%
    pull(protein)
  # compute importance scores
  proteins_s2 <- rf_out$importance %>% 
    as_tibble() %>%
    mutate(protein = rownames(rf_out$importance)) %>%
    slice_max(MeanDecreaseGini, n = num2) %>%
    pull(protein)
  ## LOGISTIC REGRESSION
  #######################
  
  # select subset of interest
  proteins_hard <- intersect(proteins_s1, proteins_s2)
  proteins_fuzzy <- union(proteins_s1, proteins_s2)
  if (intersection){
    proteins <- union(proteins_s1, proteins_s2)
  }
  else{
    proteins <- intersect(proteins_s1, proteins_s2)
  }
  
  biomarker_sstar <- training(biomarker_split) %>%
    select(group, any_of(proteins)) %>%
    mutate(class = (group == 'ASD')) %>%
    select(-group)
  
  # fit logistic regression model to training set
  fit <- glm(class ~ ., 
             data = biomarker_sstar, 
             family = 'binomial')
  
  testing_data <- testing(biomarker_split) %>%
    mutate(class = (group == 'ASD'))
  

  # evaluate errors on test set
  class_metrics <- metric_set(sensitivity, 
                              specificity, 
                              accuracy,
                              roc_auc)
  
  output_results <- testing_data %>%
    add_predictions(fit, type = 'response') %>% 
    mutate(estimate = factor(pred >0.5, levels = c(FALSE, TRUE)),
           truth = factor(class, levels = c(FALSE, TRUE))) %>%
    class_metrics(estimate = estimate,
                             truth = truth, pred,
                             event_level = 'second')
  
  actual <- testing_data$group
  predicted <- predict(fit, newdata = testing_data, type = 'response')
  roc_obj <- roc(actual, predicted, levels = c("TD", "ASD"))
  
  plot(roc_obj, 
     main = paste('ROC Curve:',  num1, num2, intersection, sep = ' '), 
     col = '#1c7ed6', 
     lwd = 3, 
     print.auc = TRUE,
     legacy.axes = TRUE)
  
  abline(a = 0, b = 1, lty = 2, col = 'darkgray')
  
  output_results$proteins_s1 <- c(num1, num1, num1, num1)
  output_results$proteins_s2 <- c(num2, num2, num2, num2)
  output_results$total_proteins <- c(length(proteins), length(proteins), length(proteins), length(proteins))
  if (intersection){
    output_results$intersection <- c('Fuzzy','Fuzzy','Fuzzy','Fuzzy')
  }
  else{
    output_results$intersection <- c('Hard','Hard','Hard','Hard')
  }
  return(output_results)
}
```

```{r}
#Testing different combinations of number of protiens and intersection type
num1 <- c(5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40)
num2 <- c(5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40)
finalResults <- data.frame(matrix(ncol = 7, nrow = 0))
colnames(finalResults) <- c('.metric', '.estimator', '.estimate', 'proteins_s1', 'proteins_s2', 'total_proteins', 'intersection')
for (i in num1){
  for (j in num2){
    finalResults <- rbind(finalResults, modelGenerators(i, j, FALSE))
    finalResults <- rbind(finalResults, modelGenerators(i, j, TRUE))
  }
}
write.csv(finalResults, file = '../data/Q3v2_results.csv')
finalResults
```
```{r}
#Comparisons of AUC to different factors
#Shows that number of proteins isn't too important for AUC
#Generally models perform best with a decent amount of proteins but not too many proteins
plot(finalResults[finalResults$intersection != 'Fuzzy' &  finalResults$.metric == 'roc_auc',]$.estimate ~ finalResults[finalResults$intersection != 'Fuzzy' &  finalResults$.metric == 'roc_auc',]$total_proteins,
     main = 'Comparing AUC Values to Protein Count for Fuzzy Intersection', ylab = 'AUC', xlab = 'Protein Count')

plot(finalResults[finalResults$intersection != 'Hard' &  finalResults$.metric == 'roc_auc',]$.estimate ~ finalResults[finalResults$intersection != 'Hard' &  finalResults$.metric == 'roc_auc',]$total_proteins,
     main = 'Comparing AUC Values to Protein Count for Hard Intersection', ylab = 'AUC', xlab = 'Protein Count')

#Shows that Fuzzy intersection on average performs worse in general
boxplot(finalResults[finalResults$.metric == 'roc_auc',]$.estimate ~ finalResults[finalResults$.metric == 'roc_auc',]$intersection,
        main = 'Comparing AUC Values to Intersection Type', ylab = 'AUC', xlab = 'Intersection')
```
